diabetes_complications.title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status

values.no: No statement that it is unrelated
values.yes: Provider says it is NOT caused by the diabetes

missed_with_link.description: Did not apply the 'with' convention, which presumes the link between diabetes and listed conditions.

linked_despite_provider.description: Linked a condition to diabetes after the provider documented it is unrelated.

missed_code_also.description: Left out the additional code the Tabular instructs (e.g., CKD stage).

redundant_manifestation.description: Added a separate code for a manifestation already captured by the combination code.

nonbillable_code.description: Reported a category/subcategory that needs more characters.

missed_complication.description: Coded diabetes without complications when a complication was documented.

coded_unsupported_complication.description: Coded a diabetic complication that was not documented.

missed_med_status.description: Left out the long-term drug use Z code.

only_one_med_code.description: Assigned only one Z code when both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used.

z794_for_type1.description: Assigned Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes, where insulin use is inherent.

coded_med_not_documented.description: Assigned a long-term drug use code that is not documented.

coded_from_med_list.description: Inferred and coded a diagnosis from a medication list.

unspecified_when_specified.description: Used an unspecified code when severity/type was documented.

scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint
Patient presents today for routine follow-up regarding known kidney impairment.

History of Present Illness
The patient reports feeling generally well since the last visit, with no new complaints of swelling or shortness of breath. The primary focus remains on the management of chronic kidney disease, specifically noted at stage 3b. He denies any recent changes in diet or activity level. He reports adequate fluid intake and continues to monitor his blood pressure as instructed.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Furosemide 20 mg daily

Exam
Vitals are stable, with blood pressure reading of 138/84 mmHg. Cardiac exam reveals regular rhythm with no murmurs or rubs. Pulmonary exam is clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdominal exam is soft and non-tender. Skin exam reveals no rashes or signs of acute distress.

Chronic kidney disease, stage 3b.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. Follow up in three months to recheck labs and vital signs. Patient educated on maintaining a low-sodium diet and ensuring adequate hydration status.
